coverage: A manually reviewed starter collection from one 2017 HN discussion. Not a comprehensive index of Hacker News.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
books.description: A broad foundation in intelligent agents, search, reasoning, learning, and decision-making.

recommendations.threadTitle: Ask HN: Best books on AI?
recommendations.threadContext: The asker wanted practical AI books without much prior knowledge. Replies debate the need for theory and mathematical foundations.
recommendations.author: arihant
recommendations.quote: You cannot really go practical in AI without academic rigor.
recommendations.context: Recommends this first, followed by Deep Learning. The recommendation explicitly includes academic study.

books.caveat: The discussion is from 2017; no particular edition is established by this excerpt.

books.title: Deep Learning

recommendations.threadTitle: Ask HN: Best books on AI?
recommendations.threadContext: The asker wanted practical AI books without much prior knowledge. Replies debate the need for theory and mathematical foundations.
recommendations.author: arihant
recommendations.quote: It is amazing how approachable both books are for beginners, but you will be diving a lot into academic stuff as you go along.

books.title: Paradigms of Artificial Intelligence Programming
books.description: Classic AI programs as a route into Common Lisp and the craft of programming.

recommendations.threadTitle: Ask HN: Best books on AI?
recommendations.threadContext: The asker wanted practical AI books without much prior knowledge. Replies debate the need for theory and mathematical foundations.
recommendations.author: nabla9
recommendations.quote: PAIP is one of most elegant and timeless books for both programming and old school AI.
recommendations.context: A reply clarifies the full title and compares its programming depth with AIMA’s broader coverage.

books.caveat: Other replies question its relevance to contemporary AI. Read it for programming and classical techniques, rather than current model architectures.
